intro_s1_body1:
Residential parking needs are changing. How should we manage limited curbside space as our city grows? Explore different parking rules and see the consequences. What works? What doesn't?

This tool illustrates the trade-offs on a fictional street. It does not predict conditions on your street and the options do not reflect changes proposed by the City of Edmonton.
intro_s1_body2: Parking is always a balance and there are no right or wrong answers. Allow 3 to 5 minutes
intro_s1_privacy: Personal information is collected for decision-making under Section 4(c) of the Protection of Privacy Act (POPA).
intro_s1_subtitle: One street. Many needs. What would you prioritize?
intro_s2_curb_desc: Residents, visitors, and delivery vans share street spots.

intro_s2_private_desc: Some homes have parking in a garage, driveway or parking lot. Others have limited or no private parking.
intro_s2_street_desc: Residents, visitors and service providers share the available street parking.
intro_s3_bullet1: Answer the questions and watch how your choices impact activity on the street.
intro_s3_bullet2: Read the benefits and trade-offs related to each choice. You can go back and try different options.
intro_s3_body2: You can see if parking spots open up, or if cars start circling.
intro_s3_summary: This helps you see how each parking rule affects your neighbourhood street.

q1_hint_a: Drivers who park on the street pay permit fees. This covers program costs and encourages people with driveways to park off the street.
q1_hint_b: Because street parking is free, more vehicles park on the street.
q1_option_a: People who use parking through pay-per-use fees and parking permits.
q1_question: Residential parking programs cost money to operate. Who should pay for them?
q2_hint_a: Limits acceptable parking to your immediate block to keep vehicles within a short walking distance.
q2_hint_b: Increases available parking options by extending acceptable parking distance into the wider neighbourhood.
q2_question: When parking on the street near your home, what would you consider reasonably close?
q3_hint_a: Homes can only get permits for up to two street-parked cars. Extra vehicles must park in private driveways or garages.
q3_hint_b: Homes can get permits for 3 or more vehicles, so more cars end up parked along the curb.
q3_question: In neighbourhoods where street parking is in high demand, should there be a limit on parking permits per household?
q4_hint_a: Allows visitors, family, and service providers equal access to park near the home they are visiting.
q4_hint_b: Prioritizes street parking for residents, reducing competition from visitor and service vehicles.
q4_question: When street parking is in high demand, should visitors and service providers (e.g., cleaners and contractors) have the same opportunity as residents to park on the block they are visiting?
q5_hint_a: Expands parking choices on nearby residential streets for patients, students, and event attendees.
q5_hint_b: Protects nearby residential street parking for residents and guests near major destinations.
q5_question: When people visit hospitals, post-secondary institutions and event venues, should they be able to use nearby residential streets for parking (within a few blocks)?
q6_hint_a: Prioritizes street parking permits for households with fewer off-street parking alternatives.
q6_hint_b: Ensures equal permit eligibility for all households regardless of their private parking arrangements.
q6_option_a: Yes households with no private parking should get priority for permits
q6_option_b: No, households should have the same eligibility, whether or not they have private parking.
q6_question: Should access to private parking affect who can get a permit? Consider all households, including those in houses, townhomes and apartments. Private parking means a driveway, garage or other off-street parking space.

q0_option_a: Enter Postal Code (e.g. T5J 2R7), Neighbourhood, or Street Address
q0_hint_a: Identifies your neighbourhood street typology (Mature Laned, Infill & Duplex, Suburban Front Driveway, or Modern Townhome) to calibrate live curbside stall capacity.
q0_gain_a: Customizes the visual street simulation to match the exact parking dynamics of your neighbourhood (garage lanes, curb cuts, density).
q0_cost_a: Requires entering postal code or address (protected under Section 4(c) of POPA).
q0_rationale_a: Customizes visual street simulations to match the exact parking dynamics of the respondent's neighbourhood
q0_option_b: Prefer not to share location (Opt Out)
q0_hint_b: Skips location detection and loads Edmonton standard Mature Laned benchmark street.
q0_gain_b: 100% anonymous survey participation without disclosing any geographical or postal information.
q0_cost_b: Simulation uses the city-wide benchmark rather than your specific neighbourhood street layout.
q0_rationale_b: Enables anonymous survey participation without disclosing geographical or postal information
q1_gain_a: Costs are covered by people using the program, rather than through property taxes.
q1_cost_a: Fees add to users’ parking costs, including for people with no private parking.
q1_rationale_a: Ensures program operating costs are paid directly by users rather than through property taxes
q1_gain_b: People can use the program without paying separate parking fees, reducing the direct cost of access.
q1_cost_b: Program costs are shared through property taxes, including by people who do not use the parking.
q1_rationale_b: Reduces direct costs to users by funding the program through property taxes instead of separate fees
q2_gain_a: A short distance between your vehicle and home
q2_cost_a: Fewer spaces meet your preferences and your block may be full even when parking is available nearby.
q2_rationale_a: Limits acceptable parking distance to the immediate block to keep vehicles close to home
q2_gain_b: More possible spaces fall within the distance you consider acceptable.
q2_cost_b: You may have a longer walk between your vehicle and home.
q2_rationale_b: Expands acceptable parking distance to the wider neighbourhood to increase available parking options
q3_gain_a: Limiting permits can reduce competition for street parking, improving availability for other residents and visitors.
q3_cost_a: Households with more vehicles than permits would need other parking arrangements, which may be difficult if they have limited or no private parking
q3_rationale_a: Reduces competition for street parking to improve availability for other residents and visitors
q3_gain_b: Households can obtain permits for all eligible vehicles, accommodating households with multiple drivers.
q3_cost_b: More vehicles may compete for the same spaces, making parking near home harder to find.
q3_rationale_b: Accommodates households with multiple drivers by allowing permits for all eligible vehicles
q4_gain_a: Family, friends and people providing services can use available spaces close to the home they’re visiting.
q4_cost_a: Residents face more competition for those spaces and more vehicles are parked on the street.
q4_rationale_a: Allows family, friends, and service providers to park conveniently close to the homes they visit
q4_gain_b: Residents have priority for nearby spaces, reducing traffic and competition from visitor vehicles.
q4_cost_b: Visitors and service providers may need to park farther away, making visits less convenient.
q4_rationale_b: Prioritizes residents for nearby spaces by reducing competition from visitor vehicles
q5_gain_a: Patients, visitors, students and event attendees have more parking options within a few blocks of their destination.
q5_cost_a: Residents and their guests may face more competition for spaces and need to park farther away.
q5_rationale_a: Expands parking options for patients, students, visitors, and event attendees near major destinations
q5_gain_b: Residents and their guests face less competition for nearby spaces from people visiting these destinations.
q5_cost_b: People visiting nearby destinations have fewer street parking options and may need to park farther away, or use other parking facilities
q5_rationale_b: Protects residential street parking from institutional and event venue visitor spillover
q6_gain_a: Prioritizes households with fewer alternatives to street parking, regardless of housing type.
q6_cost_a: Households with private parking may have less access to permits, even when the parking does not meet all their needs.
q6_rationale_a: Prioritizes street parking permits for households with no private off-street parking options
q6_gain_b: Households have the same opportunity to obtain permits, regardless of their private parking arrangements
q6_cost_b: Households without private parking receive no additional priority and may face more competition for limited permits
q6_rationale_b: Ensures equal permit eligibility for all households regardless of private parking availability
